questions.question:
Which of the following pair of types of climate-area is NOT correct?

I. Semi-arid steppe climate - Punjab

II. Monsoon with dry summer - Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Punjab:**

 
 
• Punjab is located in** India's north-western region.**
 
• **Extreme heat and extreme cold **are what shape the climate in Punjab.
 
• Heavy rainfall falls in the area close to the **Himalayan foothills**.
 
• The area, which is far from the **hills, has high temperatures and little rainfall.**
 
• **Punjab is characterised by **Bwhw (Semi-arid steppe climate) type of climate.
 
 

***Hence I is correct.***

 
• **Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu:**

 
 
• The Bay of Bengal branch of the **southwest monsoon runs parallel** to the coast of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is located in the** Arabian Sea** branch of the** southwest monsoon rainshadow.**
 
• The Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu is characterised by **As (**Monsoon with dry summer**) type of climate**.
 
 

*Hence II is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India experiences **monsoon-like weather.**
 
• Since the majority of the nation is located within the** tropics, the entire nation **experiences** tropical monsoon weather.**
 
• Additionally, the** south-west and north-east monsoons **have an impact on the climate.
 
• The** two main elements** that affect India's climate are the** location of mountain ranges and the direction of winds** that bring rain. 
 
• The primary defining trait of **Indian climate is the alternation of seasons**.
 
• The **highest rainfall** in the world is recorded in **Meghalaya, India, **at a site named **Mawsynram. **
 
• **Jaisalmer, in Rajasthan,** may experience a year without any rain at all.

questions.question: In 1905, who concluded with Thomas Chamberlain that the planets of the Solar System originated from an encounter between the Sun and another star?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Forest Moulton**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Forest Moulton** concluded with Thomas Chamberlain in 1905 that the planets of the Solar System originated from an encounter between the Sun and another star.
 
• This theory is known as the Chamberlin-Moulton planetesimal hypothesis.
 
• According to this hypothesis, a close encounter between the Sun and a passing star resulted in the ejection of material that eventually coalesced to form the planets.
 
• This was one of the early scientific attempts to explain the formation of the Solar System.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inge Lehmann** was a Danish seismologist who discovered the Earth's inner core.
 
• **Charles Lyell** was a British geologist known for his work in establishing the principles of geology.
 
• **James Hutton** was a Scottish geologist, often referred to as the father of modern geology.

questions.question: Which is the most widely accepted model to explain the formation and evaluation of the solar system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nebular hypothesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nebular hypothesis:-**

 
 
• **The nebular hypothesis proposes that the solar system formed from a giant cloud of gas and dust called a nebula.**
 
• This nebula was mostly composed of hydrogen, with smaller amounts of helium and other elements.
 
• The nebula was also very cold, with temperatures around -270 degrees Celsius (-454 degrees Fahrenheit). 
 
• Over time, the nebula began to collapse under its own gravity. As the nebula collapsed, it spun faster and faster.
 
• This spinning caused the nebula to flatten out into a disk, with the sun forming at the center of the disk.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gas hypothesis:-**

 
 
• It was proposed by Immanuel Kant in the 18th century.
 
• **It proposed that the solar system formed from a cloud of gas that had been heated by a passing star.**
 
• The heat from the star caused the gas to expand, and this expansion eventually caused the cloud to collapse.
 
• As the cloud collapsed, it spun faster and faster, and this spinning caused the cloud to flatten out into a disk.
 
• The sun formed at the center of the disk, and the planets formed from the remaining material in the disk.
 
 
 
• **Solar hypothesis:-**
 
 
• It was proposed by René Descartes in the 17th century.
 
• **It proposed that the solar system formed from a vortex of matter that was ejected from the sun. **
 
• The vortex of matter eventually cooled and solidified, and this solidified matter formed the planets and other bodies in the solar system.
 
 
 
• **Cloud hypothesis:-**
 
 
• It was proposed by Thomas Wright in the 18th century.
 
• **It proposed that the solar system formed from a cloud of dust that had been ejected from a much larger star. **
 
• The cloud of dust eventually cooled and solidified, and this solidified matter formed the planets and other bodies in the solar system.

questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT **one of the major tectonic plates of the earth?

options.text: Africa with the eastern Atlantic floor plate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nazca plate**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Tectonic Plates

 
 
• A tectonic plate (also called a lithospheric plate) is a massive, irregularly-shaped slab of solid rock, generally composed of both continental and oceanic lithosphere.
 
• The lithosphere includes the crust and top mantle with its thickness range varying between 5-100 km in oceanic parts and about 200 km in the continental areas.
 
• The concept of Tectonic Plates was first introduced in **1967**.
 
• A tectonic plate may be a continental plate or an oceanic plate, depending on which of the two occupies the larger portion of the plate.
 
• The Pacific plate is largely an oceanic plate whereas the Eurasian Plate is a continental plate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Major and Minor Plates

 
 
• The Earth’s lithosphere is divided into seven major and some minor plates.
 
• Young Fold Mountain ridges, oceanic trenches, and/or transform faults surround the major plates. These include:
 
• The Antarctic (and the surrounding oceanic) plate
 
• The North American plate (with the western Atlantic floor separated from the South American plate along with the Caribbean islands)
 
• The South American plate (with the western Atlantic floor separated from the North American plate along with the Caribbean islands)
 
• The Pacific plate
 
• The India-Australia-New Zealand plate
 
• Africa with the eastern Atlantic floor plate
 
• Eurasia and the adjacent oceanic plate
 
 
 
• Some important minor plates include:
 
 
• Cocos plate: Between Central America and the Pacific plate
 
• Nazca plate: Between South America and the Pacific plate
 
• Arabian plate: Mostly the Saudi Arabian landmass
 
• Philippine plate: Between the Asiatic and Pacific plate
 
• Caroline plate: Between the Philippine and Indian plates (North of New Guinea)
 
• Fuji plate: North-east of Australia
 
• Juan De Fuca plate: South-East of North American Plate.
 
 
 
• Hence, Option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
Identify whether the given statements about an earthquake are correct or incorrect.

**Statement 1:** When the stress on the edge overcomes the friction, there is an earthquake that releases energy in waves that travel through Earth's crust and causes the shaking that we feel.

**Statement 2:** An earthquake cannot be identified as a foreshock until after a larger earthquake in the same area occurs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Both Statements 1 and 2 are correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Earthquake occurs when movement of plates __generates stress which overcomes the friction. The release of energy causes __shaking of earth__ known as Earthquake. 
 
• The Foreshock is an earthquake that comes before the larger seismic event, known as the Mainshock.
 
• The__ __smaller earthquakes which comes after the Mainshock are called Aftershocks.
 
• Foreshocks helps in understanding the stress in the Earth's crust and can provide insights for the larger mainshock.
 
• The Mainshock is the most significant earthquake in a sequence that release the majority stress

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__ **

 
• **Earthquake releases two types of waves:**** ****Body waves and Surface Waves.**
 
• Body waves are Classified as **P-waves and S-waves**. S-waves are more harmful.
 
• Surface waves are classified as** Love waves and Rayleigh waves.**
 
• The point where earthquake arises is known as **Focus or Hypocentre**.
 
• The vertical point of Focus on the surface of Earth is called **Epicentre**.

questions.question: The age of the Earth is currently thought to be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.5 billion years.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The age of the earth is **approx. 4.543 billion years**.
 
• The **oldest rocks** on Earth found to date are the **Acasta Gneiss in northwestern Canada** near the **Great Slave Lake**, which are 4.03 billion years old.
 
• Researchers in **Australia **found the oldest **mineral grains** on Earth.
 
• These **tiny zirconium silicate** crystals have ages that reach 4.3 billion years, making them the oldest terrestrial materials found on Earth so far.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The age of rocks is determined by **radiometric dating**.
 
• In **1862, the physicist William Thomson** published calculations that fixed the age of Earth.
 
• Radiometric dating calculates an age in years for geologic materials by measuring the presence of a short-life radioactive element.
 
• Radiocarbon dating uses the carbon isotopes **carbon-14 and carbon-12.**

questions.question:
Which of the following sets of statements are correct about Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?

a. The ITCZ is a broad trough of low pressure in equatorial latitudes.

b. This is where the northeast and the southeast trade winds converge.

c. The ITCZ is the equatorial trough normally positioned about 5°N of the equator and remain there throughout the year.

d. The ITCZ moves over to the plane of Ganga in Summer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) **a, b, and d. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ITCZ is a broad trough of **low pressure **that generally exists close to the **equator** on Earth. **So statement (a) is correct.**
 
• This is the meeting point of the** northern and southern hemispheres' trade winds,** which cause frequent thunderstorms and a lot of rain. **So statement (b) is also correct.**
 
• This zone is known for its significant movement across the equator following the sun’s zenith point, which explains its shift towards the **Ganga plain** in the summer. **So statement (d) is correct**.
 
• The statement that the ITCZ remains around 5°N of the equator throughout the year is incorrect, as the **ITCZ moves north and south of the equator seasonally,** influenced by the sun's position, rather than staying fixed near 5°N. This makes **statement (c) as incorrect.**
 
• This dynamism is a key characteristic of the ITCZ, influencing **rainfall patterns in tropical regions**.

Hence the correct option combination is **a,b and d.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **Equator**__ is defined as **0 degrees latitude**.
 
• The **Tropic of Cancer** is roughly **23 degrees north**.
 
• The **Tropic of Capricorn** is roughly **23 degrees south.**
 
• The approximate locations of the **Antarctic and Arctic circles** are **66 degrees south and north**, respectively.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct according to plate tectonics?

options.text: A tectonic plate is a massive, regularly-shaped slab of solid rock.
The theory of plate tectonics proposes that the earth’s lithosphere is divided into seven major and some minor plates.
Plates move vertically over the asthenosphere as rigid units.
A tectonic plate is composed of only continental lithosphere.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The theory of plate tectonics proposes that the earth’s lithosphere is divided into seven major and some minor plates.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The theory of plate tectonics proposes that the earth’s lithosphere is divided **into seven major and some minor plates**.
 
• **Major plates are**:
 
 
• African plate,
 
• Antarctic plate,
 
• Eurasian plate,
 
• Indo-Australian plate,
 
• North American plate,
 
• Pacific plate and
 
• South American plate.
 

 
 
• **Hence Statement 2 is correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb6ce0b9a80bc6d98b22a089420b1abf8c5b9ed04bc4641130e138fed7177f4e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Oceanic and continental plates come together, spread apart, and interact at boundaries all over the planet.
 
• Each type of plate boundary generates distinct geologic processes and landforms.
 
• At convergent boundaries, plate collides with one another.
 
• Herry Hess first attempt to explain the problems of continental drift theory using the plate tectonic mechanism during the 1960s. 
 
• The mobile rock beneath the rigid plates is believed to be moving in a circular manner.
 
• The heated material rises to the surface, spreads and begins to cool, and then sinks back into deeper depths.
 
• This cycle is repeated over and over to generate what scientists call a convection cell or convective flow.
 
• Heat within the earth comes from two main sources: radioactive decay and residual heat.
 
• Arthur Holmes first considered this idea in the 1930s, which later influenced Harry Hess’s thinking about seafloor spreading.
 
• The slow movement of the hot, softened mantle that lies below the rigid plates is the driving force behind the plate movement
 
• The plate tectonic mechanism also becomes helpful to explain the mountain building, the origin of the earthquake, and Seafloor spreading

questions.question: When was the Indian Meteorological Department,Which collects data on temperature, rainfall, wind, etc., and makes weather forecasts, established by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1875**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The India Meteorological Department (IMD), **established by the **Government of India in 1875**, serves as the **nation's primary National Meteorological Service**, overseeing** all meteorology-related matters**.
 
• Operating under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, IMD holds primary responsibility for meteorological observations, weather forecasting, and seismology in the country. 
 
• Headquartered in Delhi, IMD manages a vast network of observation stations spread across India and Antarctica, ensuring comprehensive coverage.
 
• Regional offices located in Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata, Nagpur, Guwahati, and New Delhi facilitate efficient operations and localized services.
 
• Recognized as one of the six Regional Specialised Meteorological Centres by the World Meteorological Organisation, IMD plays a crucial role in forecasting and managing tropical cyclones in the Northern Indian Ocean region.
 
• This includes issuing warnings and naming cyclones affecting areas such as the Malacca Straits, the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea, and the Persian Gulf.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• After India gained independence on 27 April 1949, IMD became a member of the **World Meteorological Organisation**.
 
• The agency's importance has grown significantly due to the crucial role of monsoon rains in Indian agriculture.
 
• It is instrumental in forecasting the annual monsoon and monitoring its progress across the country each season.
 
• The IMD is led by the Director General of Meteorology, presently Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.
 
• In January 2016, IMD initiated the System of Aerosol Monitoring and Research (SAMAR) to analyze the concentration of Black carbon, radiative properties of aerosols, environmental visibility, and their climatic impacts. SAMAR comprises a network of 16 aethalometers, 12 sky radiometers, and 12 nephelometers.

questions.question: At normal temperature and atmospheric pressure, ______ has a density of 1.87 kg/m³ , which is 1.5 times heavier than air and exists as a liquid below the critical temperature of 31°C.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **At normal temperature and atmospheric pressure, CO₂ has a density of 1.87 kg/m³, which is 1.5 times heavier than air.**
 
• This means that CO₂ will sink to the ground and collect in low-lying areas.
 
• CO₂ also exists as a liquid below the critical temperature of 31°C.
 
• This means that CO₂ can be liquefied by simply cooling it down to a temperature below 31°C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrogen:-**

 
 
• **It is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe. **
 
• It is a colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas that is highly flammable.
 
• Hydrogen is found in water, natural gas, and petroleum.
 
• It is used in a variety of applications, including fuel cells, rocket fuel, and the production of fertilizer and chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Lithium:-**
 
 
• **It is a soft, silvery-white alkali metal that is the lightest solid element. **
 
• It is highly reactive and is easily oxidized. Lithium is found in rocks and minerals, and it is extracted from brine deposits.
 
• It is used in a variety of applications, including batteries, ceramics, and medicines.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen:-**
 
 
• **It is a colorless, odorless, and non-flammable gas that makes up about 78% of the Earth's atmosphere. **
 
• It is essential for life and is found in proteins, DNA, and RNA.
 
• Nitrogen is also used in a variety of applications, including fertilizers, explosives, and the production of ammonia and other chemicals.

questions.question: What percentage of earth’s water is fresh?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **2.7 percent** of earth’s water is fresh.
 
• Only 2.5% of this water is freshwater, and 98.8% of that water is in ice (except ice in clouds) and groundwater.
 
• Less than 0.3% of all freshwater is in rivers, lakes, and the atmosphere, and an even smaller amount of the Earth's freshwater (0.003%) is contained within biological bodies and manufactured products.
 
• Out of the total water present on the planet earth, the majority is in the form of **seas and oceans (more than 97%)** and is termed as a **saline water**.
 
• The remaining water is termed as **freshwater.**
 
• The decreasing order of proportion of freshwater in different forms is as follows:
 
 
• snow caps, icebergs, and glaciers > groundwater > freshwater lakes > atmosphere > rivers

questions.question: EI-Nino is a complex weather system that appears once every three to ______ years, bringing drought, floods and other weather extremes to different parts of the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• El Nino refers to the **unusual warming **of the **central and east-central equatorial Pacific Ocean** which affects global weather.
 
• The warmer waters of the Pacific Ocean cause the winds in various regions to reverse, like the trade winds that come towards India.
 
• It is a complex weather system that appears once every **three to seven years**, bringing **drought, floods, and other weather extremes** to different parts of the world.
 
• Over **India**, the El Nino has usually been the **harbinger of drought** and the **La Nina of rain**.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There is also an opposite of an El Nino, called La Nina means The Little Girl in Spanish.
 
• This refers to times when the waters of the tropical eastern Pacific are colder than normal and trade winds blow more strongly than usual.
 
• Collectively, El Nino and La Nina are parts of an oscillation in the ocean-atmosphere system called the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, or ENSO cycle.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

questions.question: What is Kalbaisakhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pre monsoon showers and thunderstorms.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Kalbaisakhi**:-

 
 
• It is also known as Bordoi Sila in Assam.
 
• **It is a localized rainfall and thunderstorm event that occurs in Bangladesh and eastern India, particularly in the states of Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Tripura, Assam, and West Bengal, during the pre-monsoon season, typically from April to May.**
 
• **It is characterized by sudden strong winds, pre monsoon showers and thunderstorms.**
 
• The term "Kalbaisakhi" is derived from the Odia and Bengali languages.
 
• In Odia, "Kal" means "black" or "dark" and "Baisakh" refers to the Bengali month of Baisakh, which corresponds to April-May in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The name reflects the sudden and intense nature of these storms, which can bring dark clouds and heavy rain.

questions.question: What is the name of the large supercontinent that existed 200 million years ago when all the continents were together?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **__Pangea__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pangea **is the name of the large supercontinent that existed **200 million years **ago when all the continents were together.
 
• **Pangaea, **the supercontinent, emerged during the **late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic periods.**
 
• One notable segment of this ancient supercontinent was Gondwana Land, situated in the **southern part of Pangaea**, with Angara Land occupying the northern region.
 
• Initially, Gondwana was not classified as a supercontinent due to the separation of landmasses such as Baltica, Laurentia, and Siberia.
 
• Gondwana eventually emerged as the largest continental landmass during the** Paleozoic Era**, spanning approximately 100,000,000 square kilometers, or about one-fifth of Earth's surface.
 
• Areas once part of Gondwana continue to exhibit shared botanical and zoological characteristics that endure to the present day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A supercontinent** is a vast landmass comprising most or all of **Earth's continents**.
 
• Some geologists characterize a supercontinent as an amalgamation of once-disparate continents.
 
• These supercontinents have cyclically formed and fragmented over the course of Earth's history.
 
• The most recent supercontinent, Pangea, coalesced between 450 and 320 million years ago.
 
• Its fragmentation commenced approximately 185 million years ago and continues to disperse to this day.

questions.question:
Choose the correct statement(s) related to ‘continentality’.

a. The sea exerts a moderating influence on climate.

b. As the distance from the sea increases, the people experience extreme weather conditions.

c. As one goes from the surface of the earth to higher altitudes, the atmosphere becomes less dense and temperature decreases.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: A and B only**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 

__
 
• **The sea exerts a moderating influence on climate:**

 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• Large bodies of water, such as seas and oceans, have a high capacity for heat storage and release. This results in a moderating effect on the climate of coastal areas, leading to milder winters and cooler summers.
 
• For example, London (close to the Atlantic Ocean) has a more moderate climate compared to Moscow, which is further inland.
 
 
 
• **As the distance from the sea increases, the people experience extreme weather conditions:**
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• Continental regions, which are far from the sea, often experience more extreme temperature variations. This is because they lack the moderating influence of the ocean, resulting in hotter summers and colder winters.
 
• For example, areas like Siberia (inland Russia) and Central Canada exhibit extreme temperatures due to their distance from the moderating effects of large water bodies.
 
 
 
• **As one goes from the surface of the earth to higher altitudes, the atmosphere becomes less dense and temperature decreases:**
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**.
 
• Although this statement is true in a general sense (i.e., atmospheric density decreases with altitude and temperatures drop in a typical troposphere), it is not directly related to the concept of 'continentality', which deals specifically with distance from large water bodies.
 
• This concept is more relevant to the study of vertical climate zones and phenomena like the adiabatic lapse rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Continentality:**

 
 
• Continentality refers to the climatic condition of areas located far from the influence of the ocean, leading to greater temperature extremes.
 
• Land heats up and cools down more quickly than water, which is why inland areas experience more significant temperature variations compared to coastal areas.
 
 
 
• **Moderating Influence of the Sea:**
 
 
• The ocean's ability to store and release large amounts of heat moderates the climate of coastal regions.
 
• This effect can reduce the severity of temperature extremes, leading to more stable and mild climates in areas close to large bodies of water.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Altitude on Climate:**
 
 
• While altitude does indeed affect temperature and atmospheric density, it is a separate concept from continentality.
 
• Higher altitudes generally experience cooler temperatures and thinner air compared to sea level, which is a factor considered in vertical climate zonation.

questions.question: Which winds blow across the Asian continent at latitudes north of the Himalayas roughly parallel to the Tibetan highlands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jet streams**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jet streams** are **high-altitude winds** that traverse the **Asian continent **above the latitudes north of the Himalayas, running roughly parallel to the **Tibetan highlands**.
 
• The Tibetan highlands act as a dividing line, splitting the jet streams into north and south branches, with the northern branch significantly influencing **winter weather patterns** in India.
 
• These fast-flowing air currents are typically observed at altitudes of up to 3 km in the lower troposphere.
 
• Furthermore, at higher elevations, between 9 to 13 km above the Earth's surface, westerly winds persistently blow across Western and Central Asia from west to east.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The trade winds** are consistent winds that blow from east to west, occurring just north and south of the equator.
 
• **Southwest winds** carry warm air from the tropics and gradually cool as they travel northward over the sea.
 
• Northwest winds originate from the northwest direction and blow in a southeastward direction.

questions.question: What type of climate is found in North Western Europe, West Coast of North America, North of California, Southern Chile, South-eastern Australia and New Zealand?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Marine west coast climate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The marine west coast climate **is typically found poleward from the **Mediterranean climate **on the western coastlines of continents.
 
• Major regions experiencing this climate include **Northwestern Europe,** the west coast of North America, northern California, southern Chile, southeastern Australia, and New Zealand.
 
• Characterized by its marine influence, this climate exhibits moderate temperatures, with winters often milder than expected for their latitude.
 
• **Summer** mean temperatures generally range from **15° to 20°C**, while winter temperatures typically fall between 4° and 10°C.
 
• In this climate, both annual and daily temperature ranges tend to be small. Precipitation is distributed evenly throughout the year, with rainfall occurring frequently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cold Snow Forest Climate: **This climate occurs in a vast international area in the northern hemisphere, spanning Europe, Asia, and North America. It is characterized by relatively wet conditions and is located poleward of the climates.
 
• **Subtropical Steppe Climate:** Subtropical steppe areas experience a short wet period alongside a Mediterranean-like climate. This climate can be found across various regions, including Europe, Asia, Australia, and North America. In Asia, it is observed in places like Rajasthan, particularly in the Thar Desert, India, and the Arabian Peninsula.
 
• **Tropical Wet and Dry Climate: **Extensive Tropical Wet and Dry climate regions are located in the northern and southern areas of the Amazon forest in Brazil, as well as adjoining parts of Bolivia and Paraguay in South America, Sudan, and the southern regions of Central Africa.

questions.question: The depositional pattern of CaCO₃ and other materials that extend upwards from the floor of a limestone cavern is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stalagmite**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **stalagmite** is a type of rock formation that rises from the floor of a cave due to the accumulation of material deposited on the floor from ceiling drippings.
 
• These formations are typically composed of **calcium carbonate (CaCO3)** and other minerals.
 
• Stalagmites grow upwards from the floor, as opposed to **stalactites**, which hang from the ceiling of caves.
 
• The growth of stalagmites is influenced by the rate of dripping water and the concentration of minerals in the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stalactites** and stalagmites are often found in pairs, with stalactites hanging from the ceiling and stalagmites growing from the ground directly below them.
 
• When a stalactite and stalagmite meet, they form a column or pillar.
 
• The formation of these structures can take thousands of years, depending on the environmental conditions within the cave.
 
• Both formations are key attractions in many limestone caves around the world, drawing interest from tourists and geologists alike.

questions.question: How many controls are there globally that influence the climate of a particular zone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Six major controls influence the climate of a particular zone globally:
 
 
• **Latitude:** The latitude of a location determines the angle at which sunlight strikes the Earth's surface. Locations closer to the equator receive more direct sunlight and have warmer temperatures, while locations farther from the equator receive less direct sunlight and have cooler temperatures.
 
• **Altitude**: Altitude refers to the elevation of a location above sea level. As altitude increases, the atmosphere becomes thinner, and air pressure decreases. This reduced air pressure leads to cooler temperatures.
 
• **Distance from the sea:** Land heats up and cools down more quickly than water. Coastal areas tend to have more moderate temperatures than inland areas because the ocean moderates the temperature fluctuations.
 
• **Ocean currents:** Ocean currents transport heat around the globe. Warm ocean currents can bring warmer temperatures to coastal areas, while cold ocean currents can bring cooler temperatures.
 
• **Topography:** Topography refers to the physical features of a landscape, such as mountains and valleys. Mountains can block wind and precipitation patterns, while valleys can trap heat and moisture.
 
• **Prevailing winds:** Prevailing winds are the dominant wind patterns in a region. They can bring warm or cold air masses to an area, influencing the local climate.
